Title: Pinpoint the Narrative stage as the primary recurrent locus of company-first hierarchy drift
Description: Across experiments 007–009 the Narrative stage most often shows the first visible editorial shift away from the requested company-first introduction—turning a company-led story into an orchestration/product-led narrative. A focused piece would explain this pattern, give concrete run-level examples, and recommend evaluating Narrative as the primary control point before broad prompt rewrites.
Audience: Product/content owners, prompt engineers, workflow architects, and experiment designers working on Nuëyon.Compose editorial pipelines
Rationale: This is the strongest, source-grounded editorial opportunity because the report explicitly identifies Narrative as the most recurrent first failure point and provides per-run evidence. Explaining where the pipeline commonly breaks helps readers design smaller, higher-confidence interventions (and avoid over-correcting Idea or Compose alone). The piece would directly serve the report's purpose: diagnose pipeline drift and focus the next trial. It also limits assumption risk because it stays within observed localization rather than inferring internal causes.
Evidence: Cross-experiment summary: “Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift in the available records.” Specific examples cited: Experiment 007 candidates 001–002 (Narrative first), Experiment 008 A-002 (Narrative factual breach), Experiment 009 baseline 002/003 and candidates 001–003 (Narrative first visible hierarchy shifts). The report also notes exceptions (Idea or Synthesis drift in some runs) and preserves uncertainty about causation, supporting a constrained, evidence-based claim.
